Brings the cameras of an [Agent DVR](https://www.ispyconnect.com/) server (iSpyConnect, free for local
use) into Gladys: their image, the motion detected, the recording going on, whether they are switched
on, and whether the system is armed. Agent DVR's motion and alerts start scenes, with the image of the
moment, which a scene can send you. Scenes can also arm or disarm Agent DVR, start a recording and
switch cameras on or off.

Tested against a real Agent DVR server in Docker (7.0) with simulated network cameras, not yet on an
installation in service with real cameras: feedback welcome on
[GitHub](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-agentdvr/issues) or on the Gladys forum.

## What you need

- Gladys 5.1 or later.
- Agent DVR installed on a computer of the local network (Windows, Linux, macOS, Docker), reachable
  from Gladys on its web port (8090 by default). No iSpyConnect account nor subscription: everything
  goes through the local API of Agent DVR.
- The cameras already added in Agent DVR.

## Installation

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**, find **Agent DVR** and install it.
2. In its **Configuration** tab, fill in:
   - **Agent DVR address**: the address of the computer running Agent DVR, e.g. `192.168.1.20`.
     Without a port, 8090 is used; add `:port` if it was changed, or `https://` behind a reverse
     proxy.
   - **User name** and **Password**: only if Agent DVR asks for a login on its API on your network
     (sent as HTTP Basic). Usually, leave them empty.
   - **Motion check**: how often motion, recording, the armed state and new alerts are read (2, 5, 10
     or 30 seconds, 5 by default).
   - **Image refresh**: how often each camera image is sent to Gladys (from 10 seconds to 15 minutes,
     1 minute by default). Motion or an alert also sends one at once.
   - **Language of the names**: the language of the feature names given when a camera is added.
3. Save, then open the **Discovery** tab: one device per camera, and an **Agent DVR** device for the
   server. Add the ones you want.
4. **Check the connection** shows what the integration reads: the Agent DVR version, whether it is
   armed, each camera, whether it receives images and records.

## The Gladys devices

Each Agent DVR camera becomes a Gladys camera, named as in Agent DVR, with:

| Feature       | What it is                                                                   |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Image**     | The camera image, sent at the chosen pace and at once on motion or an alert. |
| **Motion**    | 1 while Agent DVR detects motion on the camera, else 0.                      |
| **Recording** | 1 during a recording. A switch: starts or stops a recording.                 |
| **Camera on** | 1 when the camera is switched on in Agent DVR, 0 when it is switched off.    |

The **Agent DVR** device stands for the server:

| Feature               | What it is                                     |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **Armed**             | 1 when Agent DVR is armed (alerts on), else 0. |
| **Cameras recording** | How many cameras are recording right now.      |

**Armed** and **Camera on** are read only, on purpose: disarming or switching a surveillance camera
off is a deliberate choice, made by a scene action or the widget, never a switch a voice assistant
would flip by mistake. A camera switched on that sends no more images to Agent DVR shows as
unreachable in Gladys.

**Cameras added with version 1.0.x**: their old **Camera on** feature was of the Gladys type
"camera enabled", which Gladys 5.2 uses as the privacy mode of the camera (at 0, Gladys refuses its
images). Open the Discovery tab of the integration and click **Update** on each camera: the feature
is replaced by the new one. Until then, the integration sets the old one to 1 once at startup, so
the images keep flowing.

## Dashboard widget

**Agent DVR camera** shows the image of a camera, motion, recording and the armed state, and three
buttons: **Record** (or **Stop recording**; **Switch the camera on** when it is off), **Disarm** (or
**Arm**) and **New image**.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **Agent DVR: motion detected**: a camera starts detecting motion, armed or not. Filter: the camera
  (empty = all). Variable: the camera name. The image of the moment is sent to Gladys first.
- **Agent DVR: alert**: Agent DVR raises an alert. It only does when **armed**, for a camera whose
  alerts are on: motion, AI object detection, a command… Filter: the camera. Variables: the camera
  name and the alert message (e.g. `Alert`). The image of the moment is sent first.
- **Agent DVR: camera offline**: a camera switched on sends no more images to Agent DVR for 30
  seconds, or Agent DVR itself stops answering. Not fired for a camera switched off.

### Actions

- **Agent DVR: arm or disarm**: arms the system (the cameras with alerts on raise alerts) or disarms
  it.
- **Agent DVR: record**: **Start** starts a recording on a camera, **Stop** stops it. Refused on a
  camera switched off.
- **Agent DVR: switch a camera on or off**: switches one camera on or off, or all of those added in
  Gladys when the camera is left empty. Output: how many cameras changed.

The core's **Send a camera image** action sends the last image of a camera: right after **Agent DVR:
motion detected** or **Agent DVR: alert**, it is the image of that moment.

### Scene ideas

- **Leaving home**: when everyone is gone, **Agent DVR: arm or disarm** on Arm, and **Agent DVR:
  switch a camera on or off** on Switch on for all; when someone is back, Disarm, and Switch off the
  indoor cameras.
- **Intrusion**: **Agent DVR: alert** on the "Garden" camera → **Send a camera image** of that camera
  to your phone.
- **Door opened at night**: an opening sensor opens → **Agent DVR: record**, Start, on the entrance
  camera; Stop two minutes later.
- **Camera lost**: **Agent DVR: camera offline** → send a message with the camera name.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Agent DVR does not answer at this address"**: open `http://<address>:8090` in a browser. Check
  the port (Server settings in Agent DVR) and that no firewall blocks Gladys.
- **"Something answers, but not like Agent DVR"**: the address or the port leads to another service.
  Enter the address of Agent DVR, without a page path.
- **"Agent DVR refuses the user name or password"**: check them, or leave them empty if Agent DVR
  asks for nothing on the local network.
- **No "alert" trigger**: Agent DVR must be armed, and alerts on for the camera (in its settings,
  Alerts tab). **Agent DVR: motion detected** does not depend on arming.
- **A camera stays unreachable**: Agent DVR receives no images from it. Check it in Agent DVR.
- **More details**: the integration logs (Integrations → Agent DVR → Logs); set `LOG_LEVEL` to
  `debug` to see each request.

## Limits

- No live video: Gladys shows images, sent at the chosen pace (Gladys keeps 12 images a minute per
  camera at most). The live stream is watched in Agent DVR.
- Motion is read every few seconds (the motion check): a very short motion between two readings may
  go unseen. Alerts, on the other hand, are all read.
- Agent DVR has no push state API usable without configuration: the integration polls it. With a
  2-second interval and many cameras, that is many small requests.
- Agent DVR microphones, PTZ, profiles and past recordings are not covered.
- One Agent DVR server per integration.
- Tested with Agent DVR 7.0 in Docker and simulated cameras, without a real installation: feedback
  welcome.

This integration is not affiliated with iSpyConnect nor Agent DVR.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Agent DVR asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Your Agent DVR server | `section` | No | Agent DVR by iSpyConnect, free for local use. Enter the address of the computer running it (port 8090 by default). Then open the Discovery tab: one device per camera, and one for the server. |
| Agent DVR address | `string` | Yes | Without a port, 8090 is used. Add https:\/\/ for a reverse proxy. |
| User name | `string` | No | Only if Agent DVR asks for a login on your network. Usually empty. |
| Password | `secret` | No |  |
| Motion check | `select` | No | How often motion, recording, the armed state and new alerts are read. |
| Image refresh | `select` | No | How often each camera image is sent to Gladys. An alarm or a new event also sends one at once. |
| Language of the names | `select` | No | Names given to the features when a camera is added (Motion, Recording…). |

## How to install Agent DVR in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Agent DVR appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/guim31/gladys-agentdvr:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/guim31/gladys-agentdvr](https://github.com/guim31/gladys-agentdvr).

Agent DVR requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Agent DVR is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core.
